contentitemdata.dancinggoat.articlepage.ArticlePageSummary: Fresh beans go stale faster than you think. Keep them away from air, light, heat, and moisture, and your coffee will taste better for longer.
contentitemdata.dancinggoat.articlepage.ArticlePageText:
Roasted coffee starts losing its aroma the day it leaves the roaster. You can't stop that, but you can slow it down a lot.

The four enemies

  • Air: use an airtight container, and keep it as full as you can.
  • Light: pick an opaque jar or keep the bag in a cupboard.
  • Heat: skip the shelf above the stove or next to the espresso machine.
  • Moisture: don't keep your daily beans in the fridge — condensation is worse than room temperature.

Buy little and often

We roast in small batches for a reason. Buy what you'll drink in two to three weeks, and grind right before you brew. If you've got extra, freeze it in small, sealed portions and only take out what you need.
